subject: Dedicated burst tiering and cooldown — proposal + questions
messages:
From: Alice Park <alice.park@acme.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Interest in Dedicated + burst add-on — throughput guarantees and cooldowns

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the product demo yesterday — Acme’s engineering team is excited about Redwood Dedicated. We have two follow-ups before we get to legal procurement: 1) how burst capacity is priced and rate-limited (we expect large batch jobs and unpredictable spiky inference during end-of-day processing), and 2) what cooldowns / pacing policies look like (we need predictable behavior so our job scheduler can plan).

Specifics from our side:
- Baseline reserved commit we’re considering: 8 GPU-equivalents (we usually size by v100/h100 equivalent).
- Burst requirement: up to +100% of baseline for short windows (15–90 minutes), peak maybe 4–6 times baseline for seconds-long spikes.
- Contract term we prefer: 12 months, with quarterly review.

Could you share:
- Burst tiering and per-hour or per-token surge rates (examples are fine),
- Any burst credit model (monthly credits vs metered surge),
- Cooldown rules (minimum time between sustained bursts, refill behavior), and
- If there’s room for a commit discount if we commit to a base and a small guaranteed burst pool.

Appreciate a clear example invoice/estimate for our expected profile.

Best,
Alice Park
Head of Procurement, Acme Corp
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Park <alice.park@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-03T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interest in Dedicated + burst add-on — throughput guarantees and cooldowns

Hi Alice — great to hear Acme liked the demo. Below is a concise breakdown of options that map to the profile you described. I attached a 1‑p PDF summary and a sample cost workbook.

Summary (baseline = 8 GPU-equivalents reserved commit):
1) Base Reserved Capacity:
   - Monthly commit: priced as $X per GPU-equivalent / month (line-item in attached workbook).
   - Throughput guarantee: baseline commit supports sustained throughput up to the provisioned pool at p95 latency target (we can specify target for your specific model—e.g., p95 token latency 120ms).

2) Burst add-on models (pick one):
   A) Metered surge (pay-as-you-go):
      - Up to 2x baseline sustained for short windows (minutes to 2 hours) charged at 2.0x the on-commit unit rate.
      - Short spikes (seconds) auto-handled by our request queueing and elastic routing; those are throttled but not charged at the 2.0x rate unless they exceed sustained thresholds.
   B) Burst credit pool (prepaid):
      - Buy a monthly burst credit pool (example: 200 GPU-minutes) priced at ~1.6x equivalent on-commit rate per minute; credits are consumed when usage exceeds baseline.
      - Credits auto-refill monthly, unused credits roll over up to 2 cycles.
   C) Guaranteed burst slab (reserved burst):
      - Add a small reserved burst slab (e.g., +25% capacity) at a discounted add-on unit price (roughly 0.5x of normal incremental price) to reduce variability and avoid metered surcharges.

3) Cooldown & surge control (policy examples):
   - Sustained burst cooldown: after any sustained burst that exceeds 30 consecutive minutes at >150% baseline, a 60-minute cooldown is applied for additional sustained bursts above that threshold.
   - Spike smoothing: second-scale spikes are handled with our elastic routing; they do not trigger cooldowns unless aggregate sustained minutes exceed the slab/credit thresholds.
   - Emergency override: customer can opt into a paid temporary override for unlimited burst for a short period (charge rate 3.5x) — useful for one-off migration runbooks.

Example pricing sketch (illustrative — see attached workbook for numbers):
- Baseline 8 GPU-eq: $BASE/month
- Metered surge: 2.0x unit rate for metered minutes beyond baseline
- Burst credits: 200 GPU-min @ ~1.6x unit rate = $CREDIT_COST/month
- Reserved burst slab (+25%): incremental monthly fee = $SLAB_FEE/month (cheaper predictable option)

Discounting: for a 12-month committed baseline + 25% reserved burst slab we can consider a 15% net discount on baseline and 10% off the slab. If you shift to a 24-month cadence we can deepen baseline discount to ~22%.

Next steps I propose:
- Tell us which add-on model you prefer (metered vs credits vs reserved slab).
- I’ll run a sample invoice (numbers filled from your expected monthly minutes) and loop in finance for an approved concession if you pick the reserved slab route.

I attached: Dedicated_Burst_Pricing_Options_v1.pdf and a sample cost workbook. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk the workbook.

Thanks — Tessa
Tessa Morgan
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
From: Alice Park <alice.park@acme.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-04T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Interest in Dedicated + burst add-on — throughput guarantees and cooldowns

Tessa — thanks for the clear breakdown. A few clarifications / asks from Acme:

1) We prefer the reserved burst slab (+25%) for predictability. Please run numbers for: baseline 8 GPU-eq + reserved slab +25%.
2) We’ll accept a 12-month term but we want a commit discount closer to 20% on baseline, and a 15% discount on the reserved slab — is that feasible?
3) Cooldown: 60-minute cooldown after 30 minutes sustained sounds reasonable, but can the cooldown be measured on rolling-window usage (so a few short repeated bursts don’t trigger it unnecessarily)? We can provide our scheduler logs to tune thresholds if needed.
4) SLA / fallback: if a requested burst cannot be honored due to capacity, what is Redwood’s fallback? We need an explicit behavior for the job scheduler (e.g., queue + wait up to 5 minutes, or fallback to hosted at our expense).

If you can get back with a sample invoice and a confirmation on the 20%/15% concession ask, we can pull legal in.

Best,
Alice
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Park <alice.park@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-05T14:30:00-08:00
Subject: Fwd: Interest in Dedicated + burst add-on — pricing concession request (need approvals)

Marissa / Ben — forwarding Acme’s request. They want baseline 8 GPU-eq + reserved burst slab (+25%) on a 12-month term, and are asking for: 20% off baseline + 15% off the reserved slab. I included Alice in case you want to see current thread.

Key negotiation points for internal approval:
- Commercial impact: at 20% baseline discount + 15% slab discount our blended ASP drops ~18% for the first year; we should verify gross margin sensitivity against expected utilization (I attached their proposed usage workbook).
- Capacity: reserved slab reduces on-demand risk; this is positive for scheduling. No additional capacity guarantees requested beyond existing throughput SLAs, but they want clear fallback behavior if bursts can’t be delivered.
- SLA fallback recommendation: offer automatic queueing for up to 5 minutes with option to fallback to Redwood Hosted at a 1.8x metered rate if queueing exceeds 5 minutes (customer pays hosted costs).

Proposed go/no-go for concession:
- Approve 20% baseline discount if Acme signs a 12-month commitment and provides a 10% upfront deposit (applied to first month).
- Approve 12% discount on reserved slab (counter to their 15%) to preserve margin; offer a 15% slab discount only if they extend to 24 months.

If you’re ok, I’ll send a formal pricing worksheet back to Alice with the counter. If you want me to include a one-time onboarding credit instead of a deeper slab discount, I can structure that as well (e.g., $Xk one-time credit).

Onboarding attachments: Acme-Proposed-MAPL.xlsx attached.

Thanks,
Tessa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-05T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Interest in Dedicated + burst add-on — pricing concession request (need approvals)

Tessa — quick thumbs up on the approach. Two minor asks before you send the counter: 1) confirm margin impact numbers in the workbook (I’ll review offline), and 2) lock fallback wording to explicitly state "fallback to hosted subject to capacity and our hosted TOS; customer will be billed at the agreed hosted surge rate."

If both look okay I approve the proposed counter (20% baseline w/ deposit, 12% slab discount, 24-month trigger for deeper slab discount).

Marissa
